content.title: Destination Light | Depth Carriers Expand a Stable Exit
content.summary: Establish one longitudinal motion axis inside a dark enclosure. Repeated slow carriers occupy near, middle, and far depth while fixed ribs prove scale; advance along the same axis as the destination light grows monotonically, then let that exit dominate the final frame.

quick_start.input_format: single distant destination light and motion axis in an enclosed space + related slow carriers across at least three depth layers + fixed ribs preserve scale and direction + destination light grows monotonically with only brief occlusion + final light dominates while edge structure proves the same space
quick_start.recommended_input: From the bottom of a dark circular archive tower, one white skylight sits far above. Bookcase ribs and reading platforms pass at distinct depths as the camera rises; the skylight expands until it dominates while dark shelving remains at the frame edges.
required_anchors: Establish one distant destination light and one unambiguous movement axis inside an enclosure.
Place related slow carriers on at least three depth planes with different apparent speeds.
Grow the same destination light monotonically while carriers may briefly occlude it.
End when light dominates but leave edge anchors long enough to prove arrival from the original enclosure.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish one longitudinal motion axis inside a dark enclosure. Repeated slow carriers occupy near, middle, and far depth while fixed ribs prove scale; advance along the same axis as the destination light grows monotonically, then let that exit dominate the final frame.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Establish one enclosed original environment with a single distant destination light on a clear movement axis. Populate at least three depth planes with repeated slow carriers that share a visual family but vary scale and lateral drift. Move the camera continuously toward the same destination while fixed structural ribs, frames or columns pass as parallax and scale evidence. Let carriers intermittently cross the light without changing its location, and make the aperture grow monotonically until it becomes the dominant field while edge structures still prove continuity. The reusable mechanism is destination-locked traversal, layered slow carriers, fixed scale ribs, monotonic light growth and enclosure-to-release payoff—not the source cathedral, underwater setting, jellyfish, coral, moonlight, architecture, colors, exact camera path, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Establish one distant destination light and one unambiguous movement axis inside an enclosure.
invariants.purpose: Gives the traversal a measurable objective.
invariants.ablation_failure: Multiple competing lights make progress unreadable.

invariants.rule: Place related slow carriers on at least three depth planes with different apparent speeds.
invariants.purpose: Makes parallax and scale visible without fast action.
invariants.ablation_failure: One flat layer cannot communicate volume.

invariants.rule: Retain fixed ribs, frames or columns as orientation and scale anchors throughout the move.
invariants.purpose: Proves continuous travel through one space.
invariants.ablation_failure: Removing all structure turns the sequence into an abstract dissolve.

invariants.rule: Grow the same destination light monotonically while carriers may briefly occlude it.
invariants.purpose: Creates a clear progress clock and anticipation.
invariants.ablation_failure: A shrinking or relocated light breaks the destination contract.

invariants.rule: End when light dominates but leave edge anchors long enough to prove arrival from the original enclosure.
invariants.purpose: Delivers release without a disconnected white frame.
invariants.ablation_failure: A hard unrelated cut loses the spatial payoff.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source underwater cathedral, arches, columns, windows, coral and exact architecture
the source jellyfish bodies, tentacles, colors, paths and depth arrangement
the source moonlike aperture, white-blue shaft and exact illumination progression
the source camera ascent, frame order, compositions, palette and 15-second timing
the source creator identity, MiniMax H3 claim, watermark and wording
